episode_title: #409 Be The Doctor, Not The Farmacist

real_qa.q: What is the difference between a pharmacist recruiter and a doctor recruiter in sales calls?
real_qa.r: A pharmacist recruiter hands over the service immediately when a client states their need, like dispensing antibiotics without diagnosis. A doctor recruiter asks diagnostic questions first to understand the real problem before proposing a solution. The doctor asks questions to determine what is truly wrong, while the pharmacist takes the client's stated need at face value and acts on it.

real_qa.q: Why did Tom win a retained finance controller recruitment over two competing agencies on contingency?
real_qa.r: Tom won because he asked diagnostic questions instead of pitching immediately. When the hiring manager said the vacancy had been open before, Tom discovered it was the third time in three years and both previous candidates left within eight months. By asking why they left and what was costing the business, Tom positioned himself as the only recruiter who understood the real problem, so the fee and business model became irrelevant.
real_qa.requete: Tom finance recruitment retained business contingency

real_qa.q: How many questions should recruiters ask during a triage call before pitching?
real_qa.r: There are 27 questions in the triage call script designed to establish that the hiring manager has budget, authority, need and timing (BANT). In a full sales call, 58 questions may be asked with the 58th being the closing question. During the triage call itself, recruiters should pitch nothing and only ask questions to diagnose the client's real needs.

real_qa.q: What should recruiters say to themselves before a client call to avoid pitching too early?
real_qa.r: Recruiters should tell themselves 'I do not pitch, I diagnose' before entering a call. This is not something to say aloud to the prospect but an internal standard to hold. It is who you decide to be before the call starts, ensuring you choose diagnosis over the pharmacy pitch approach.
real_qa.requete: I do not pitch I diagnose recruitment call

real_qa.q: What technique should recruiters use when a client says something they do not understand?
real_qa.r: When a client says something unclear, recruiters should respond with 'That is interesting. Tell me more.' and then sit in silence. Clients will keep talking and explain themselves even better. Being comfortable in silence while the client thinks is essential because the silence represents the client's thinking process, which is the whole purpose of diagnostic selling.
real_qa.requete: that's interesting tell me more recruitment silence

real_qa.q: What was the real appendicitis diagnosis that taught the recruitment principle of asking questions first?
real_qa.r: The speaker thought he had a pulled muscle during triathlon training but a doctor asked diagnostic questions, examined him, and determined he had appendicitis—warning that if his appendix burst he could get sepsis and die. The speaker did not argue or seek other opinions; he trusted the doctor's diagnosis. This illustrates that asking questions first completely changes the dynamic and authority in a room compared to just handing over the solution.
